2026-07-14. RAW CSV RETAINED (4046 telemetry samples). Unplugged, all arms LIGHT thermal, so power is valid. Energy integrated from the power curve: naive 95 J, threads-only 57 J, ENTITY Auto 51 J for the same 128 tokens - Auto uses 47% less battery, not by drawing less current (all arms ~4.3-4.6 W) but by finishing in 11.7 s against 20.8 s. Pinning reads +9% here, but n=1; the 3-run export below puts it at +2% and inside the noise.

2026-07-14. RAW CSV RETAINED (12012 telemetry samples). THREE runs per arm, every pass LIGHT thermal: the cleanest ablation evidence in the project. Decode per pass - naive 6.94/7.21/7.74, threads-only 16.2/16.0/16.1, Auto 16.4/16.6/15.7. Thread count +123%; pinning +1.9% on the median, but Auto's worst pass (15.7) is below threads-only's worst (16.0), so the distributions overlap and mean-to-mean is +0.8% - inside the noise. Phone was CHARGING: speed is valid, power is NOT, so the power columns are not-valid-charging rather than the meaningless values the raw CSV contains (it reports 18 tok/W).

2026-07-15. RAW CSV RETAINED. First UNPLUGGED three-run set: speed and power both valid, every arm started at 38.0C, LIGHT thermal throughout. Thread count +106% decode; pinning +1% on the median. Auto's third pass was a 12.0 tok/s outlier (runs: 16.0/16.7/12.0), which is why its stddev is 2.07; the median is robust to it. Known CSV defect: affinity_naive reads pinned_fast_cores, but the naive mask is the 8 fastest of 8 cores - all of them - so naive really is scheduler-equivalent; the label was corrected in source after this export.
